en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on False Speech, 4. The Training Rule on Verses:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma word-by-word to lay followers.
The lay followers lived without respect, without deference, and without proper conduct toward the monks.
Those monks who were of few desires... [as above] ...were indignant, disparaged, and complained, saying:
“How can the group-of-six monks indeed teach the Dhamma word-by-word to lay followers?
Lay followers will thus dwell without respect, without deference, and without proper conduct toward the monks.
Then those monks, having rebuked the group-of-six monks in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that you lay followers recite the Dhamma word by word;
and that the lay followers dwell without respect, without deference, and without proper conduct toward the monks?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can you, foolish men, teach the Dhamma word by word to lay followers?
Lay followers live without respect, without deference, and without proper conduct toward the bhikkhus.”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without faith, nor to the increase of the confidence of those who already have it...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:
‘If any monk should teach the Dhamma word by word to one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of expiation.’”
"But whoever" means whoever such a person...
"a bhikkhu."
...pe... this is the meaning intended here by the term "bhikkhu.
One who is "not fully ordained" (anupasampanna) refers to everyone except for a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī; the remainder is called "not fully ordained."
"By the word" means:
by the phrase, by the following phrase, by each syllable, or by each suffix.
"Phrase" means:
They establish [the words] on one side and conclude them on the other.
"Word by word" means they establish each word separately and conclude them all together.
"Word by word" means that when it is said,
"Form is impermanent," one interrupts, saying, "Run!
"By the phrasing" means...
When it is said, “Form is impermanent,” one utters the sound,
“Feeling is impermanent. Whatever constitutes the phrase, the subsequent phrase, the individual syllables,
and the individual phonemes— all this is called “by the phrase.”
"Dhamma" means that which is spoken by the Buddha, spoken by disciples, spoken by seers, spoken by deities; it is connected with the goal and connected with the Dhamma.
"Should recite" means...
If he causes [a person] who is not fully ordained to recite by the line, there is an offense of *pācittiya* for every line.
If he causes [a person] who is not fully ordained to recite by the syllable, there is an offense of *pācittiya* for every syllable.
If one causes a person who is not fully ordained to recite the Dhamma by the line, perceiving them as not fully ordained, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If one recites the Dhamma word by word to one who is not fully ordained while being in doubt, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one recites the Dhamma word by word to one who is not fully ordained while perceiving them as fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
If one recites it to one who is fully ordained while perceiving them as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one is doubtful that the person has received full ordination, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If the person has received full ordination and one perceives them as such, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
While one person is having [the text] recited from one side and another is performing the recitation (*sajjhāya*) from the other side,
he interrupts one who is mostly reciting the text from memory with fluency.
One who causes a person being reinstated to fall into a pit;
[this is not an offense] for one who is insane,
or for an initial offender.
The fourth training rule concerning reciting the Dhamma word-for-word is finished.
